stem: What is the characteristic gait and posture of a child with slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE)?

options.text: Limping with an out-toeing foot position
Walking on the balls of the feet
A stiff-legged gait with no knee flexion

explanation: Limping with an out-toeing foot position is typical of SCFE. The slipped, externally rotated hip causes the child to walk with a limp and the foot turned outward.
rationale: SCFE commonly presents with external rotation of the affected leg, producing out-toeing and a limp.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because SCFE classically causes a limp with external rotation of the hip, leading to an out-toeing foot position.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because SCFE causes external rotation and out-toeing, not in-toeing with a high-stepping gait.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because toe-walking is not the typical gait pattern in SCFE.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because SCFE does not classically present as a stiff-legged gait without knee flexion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a wide-based waddling gait is more typical of proximal muscle weakness or other gait disorders, not SCFE.

source.hint: Consider the effect of a fixed 'external rotation' deformity on the foot's direction.
